Re: Request for Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Riley Hayes  
Member ID: W890739050  
Reference number: POC-5BC96481D7-41351  
Requested service: Shoulder labral and instability repair  
CPT: 29806  
Date of denial: August 18, 2026  

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806, arthroscopic shoulder labral and instability repair. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The clinical record does support the requested procedure because it documents a structural anteroinferior labral tear, recurrent anterior instability with multiple dislocations, persistent symptoms despite substantial conservative treatment, and significant functional impairment.

The June 20, 2026 MR arthrogram demonstrated an anteroinferior labral tear, also known as a Bankart lesion, together with a small Hill-Sachs lesion. The imaging also showed glenoid bone loss under 10 percent and an intact rotator cuff. These findings are consistent with the patient’s clinical diagnosis of recurrent anterior shoulder instability and provide an anatomic basis for repair. The intact rotator cuff does not negate the documented labral injury or instability.

The clinical history further establishes medical necessity:

- The patient has experienced 14 months of recurrent instability episodes with apprehension.
- The patient has sustained three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptoms began.
- The most recent dislocation required reduction in the emergency department.
- Examination demonstrated positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing.
- The patient has been unable to return to work involving lifting and avoids overhead reaching.
- The patient completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including 18 visits from March 16, 2026, through July 6, 2026, focused on rotator cuff and scapular-stabilizer strengthening and activity modification.
- The patient used NSAIDs for approximately four months during symptom flares.
- An injection was not indicated for mechanical instability.
- The patient has full strength, but full strength does not eliminate the documented recurrent instability, positive instability testing, structural labral tear, or repeated dislocations.

Taken together, the imaging and clinical findings show a Bankart lesion associated with recurrent anterior instability and a Hill-Sachs lesion, while the prolonged failure of supervised rehabilitation and activity modification demonstrates that nonoperative treatment has not adequately resolved the condition. The requested repair is intended to address the structural labral injury and recurrent instability that are preventing normal overhead activity and return to work.

Please reconsider the denial and approve CPT 29806 based on the complete clinical record. If the denial is maintained, please provide the exact medical-necessity criteria applied to this request, including the name, version, and effective date of any InterQual, delegated-vendor, or other clinical-review criteria; identify each criterion that was considered unmet; and explain specifically why the June 20, 2026 MR arthrogram findings were considered insufficient.

I have not been provided a publicly available Sunflower or Ambetter policy specifically addressing CPT 29806 or shoulder labral and instability repair, and I am not quoting a plan policy in this appeal. Please provide the criteria actually applied to this determination so that the appeal can be evaluated against the correct standard.

Please include the attached or previously submitted records in the appeal review:

1. June 20, 2026 MR arthrogram report;
2. Orthopedic examination findings from Duval, MD;
3. Physical therapy records and discharge note documenting 18 visits from March 16, 2026, through July 6, 2026;
4. Documentation of the three anterior dislocations, including the emergency-department reduction of the most recent dislocation;
5. Medication and conservative-treatment history; and
6. Documentation of work and activity limitations.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Riley Hayes
